speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: Have you experienced any recent fever, headaches, or confusion in the past week? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count. REQUEST TEST: Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: NORMAL READINGS; Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel: Na 122 mEq/L, K 3.9 mEq/L, HCO3 24 mEq/L, BUN 21 mg/dL, Cr 0.9 mg/dL, Ca 8.5 mg/dL, Glu 105 mg/dL

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old female. The patient has been brought to the emergency room by her family due to altered mental status. The family mentions that she has been increasingly confused over the past few days. No recent head trauma or known drug use. The patient has a smoking history of 30 pack-years.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mental status changes. I also have Increased confusion, Lethargy. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning, as gastroenteritis typically presents with gastrointestinal symptoms rather than isolated mental status changes; have you experienced any seizures, stiff neck, or severe abdominal pain? REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes. REQUEST TEST: Toxicology_Screen.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrolytes: Na 122 mEq/L, K 3.9 mEq/L, HCO3 24 mEq/L, Cl 100 mEq/L (inferred standard panel), CO2 24 mmol/L (inferred), BUN 21 mg/dL, Cr 0.9 mg/dL, Glucose 105 mg/dL, Ca 8.5 mg/dL; Toxicology_Screen: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The severe hyponatremia (Na 122 mEq/L) is the likely cause of your confusion and lethargy, which does not fit with gastroenteritis. Given the normal toxicology screen and electrolyte levels, have you experienced significant nausea, vomiting, or excessive fluid intake recently? REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Patient has a history of hypertension, managed with medication. No other significant medical history is reported. Social history: Patient is a smoker with a 30 pack-year history. Drinks alcohol socially. No illicit drug use is reported.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of hypertension and significant smoking, along with the severe hyponatremia, have you noticed any changes in your vision, speech, or weakness on one side of your body? REQUEST IMAGES: Brain_MRI

speaker: Patient
text: Denies headache, seizure, vision changes, chest pain, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, recent illness, or fever.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hyponatremic Encephalopathy secondary to Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone (SIADH).
